title: Soldering Copper Pipe for Beginners: Flux, Torch, and Finishing
summary: This beginner-focused lesson from This Old House guides a first-time solderer through assembling a 3/4-inch copper pipe joint. The instructor demonstrates marking and cutting a 6-inch piece, securing it in a pipe cutter, and verifying alignment with a Sharpie. The tutorial then covers cleaning the cut ends with an emery cloth and a fitting brush, applying flux to the pipe exterior and inside the fittings, and inserting the tube fully into the fittings. After clamping the assembly, the teacher directs safety practices (safety glasses) and demonstrates heat application with a torch, waiting for flux to bubble, and applying solder to both sides so the solder wicks toward the joint. The process concludes with removing heat, cleaning the joint, and wiping away flux for a clean, leak-free connection, followed by closing remarks and a prompt to explore more videos.

sections.title: Preparation and Cutting
sections.description: The lesson marks a 6-inch piece of 3/4-inch copper pipe and demonstrates using a pipe cutter with a thumbscrew to snug the cutter, align with the mark, and rotate for the initial cut. The first revolution is described as the most important, with guidance to stay in the groove and adjust as needed to finish the cut.

sections.title: Cleaning and Deburring
sections.description: After cutting, the pipe ends are scrubbed with emery cloth until shiny. A specialized brush is used to clean the inside of fittings by inserting the brush and spinning it to remove fragments, preparing a clean mating surface on both ends.

sections.title: Fluxing and Assembly
sections.description: Flux is applied to the outside of the pipe and inside the fittings to act as a catalyst for the solder. The tube is inserted into the fittings, ensuring it bottoms properly, and the joint is clamped for stability.

sections.title: Heating and Soldering
sections.description: With safety glasses on, the torch is used to heat the joint. The assistant is instructed to heat the side of the fitting until flux bubbles, then apply solder to the opposite side, keeping the flame about an inch away. The solder is drawn toward the heated joint, and the process is repeated on the other side. The hottest part of the flame and the timing of solder contact are emphasized, followed by moving to the other joint and continuing the heating and soldering sequence.

sections.title: Finishing and Safety Notes
sections.description: The final step emphasizes wiping the joint clean after soldering and confirms the importance of a clean, finished joint. The segment ends with encouragement to explore more This Old House videos.
